product: A multi-user, account-free web application that shows the sky — every star of the Hipparcos catalog, the Sun, the Moon, the planets and Pluto, deep-sky objects, asteroids and comets — as seen from the user's location (geolocated or entered) or from the surface of another body of the Solar System, in real time by default and at any moment of the past or future within the ephemeris. Constellation lines, names and boundaries can be shown or hidden. On phones and tablets with a rear camera, the sky can be overlaid on the camera image in augmented reality. Users: curious people and amateur astronomers, on phones first, tablets and desktops second, in French or English. No accounts, no persistence, no collaboration: the server is stateless and each user's state lives in their URL, which makes any view shareable by copying the address. What good looks like: correct (validated against JPL Horizons), smooth (no stalls while time flows), honest (validity ranges and approximations always visible), light (a session costs a few megabytes), and quietly beautiful (dark, minimal, readable at night). Naming: the product name is the repository directory name; use it in the UI title, the web manifest and the README.

architecture.principles: - Skyfield (backend) is the single astronomical authority. The frontend never computes an astronomical position from first principles. It only: (a) rotates catalog unit vectors by a backend-supplied horizon rotation, (b) applies linear proper motion with backend-supplied vectors, (c) interpolates backend-supplied samples, (d) applies annual aberration to catalog directions with the backend-supplied observer velocity (first-order formula, so stars and bodies share one apparent frame), (e) applies an atmospheric-refraction correction as a function of altitude, on Earth only, with a formula validated against Skyfield. Everything else about positions, time scales and reference frames comes from the backend. - "Backend as oracle, client as propagator": the server answers deterministic, stateless, cacheable GET requests; the client owns the simulation clock and decides when it needs new data. - No accounts, no server-side sessions, no database, no persistence. All per-user state lives in the browser and in the URL. Users never share state with each other. - Vocabulary: "the reference frontend" is the client built in this repository; the API is designed so that other clients could use it. - Determinism: identical (observer, time, options) produce byte-identical responses, so responses are cacheable at every layer.
architecture.time_model: - Simulation time is a Julian Date on the TT scale (`tt`, float64), continuous, no leap seconds. The frontend propagates it: tt += speed * elapsed_real_seconds / 86400. - Modes: live (default; tt tracks the wall clock using `tt_minus_utc_seconds` supplied by the backend), paused, playing at a signed speed chosen from a configurable list (1, 10, 60, 600, 3600, 86400, 604800, 2629800, 31557600 and their negatives), plus a "now" button that returns to live mode. - Display: TT -> UTC using `tt_minus_utc_seconds` (taken from the current frame and held constant within its window; before 1972 the backend supplies TT − UT1 and the display is labelled UT), then UTC -> the user's local zone (zone offset from Intl, year and date formatted by our own formatter, see pitfalls). Calendar is proleptic Gregorian with astronomical year numbering (year 0 exists); the UI says so for dates before 1582-10-15. The ephemeris range (-13200..+17191) fits inside the JavaScript Date range. - Coverage: every data source has a validity range reported by `/meta` (ephemeris, Moon orientation kernel, MPC elements, ΔT confidence). The UI clamps the time control to the ephemeris range and shows per-feature warnings; the backend never silently extrapolates.
architecture.coordinate_frames: - Exchange frame: ICRF (J2000 equatorial axes), unit vectors [x, y, z]. - Horizon frame: local ENU at the observer, components ordered [East, North, Up]. - The backend supplies the rotation ICRF -> ENU as a unit quaternion per time sample (Hamilton convention, v_enu = q * v_icrf * q⁻¹), computed from Skyfield `rotation_at(t)` on `GeographicPosition` (Earth, WGS84) or `PlanetTopos` (other bodies, IAU frames from the PCK kernel), after converting Skyfield's left-handed north-east-up matrix to ENU (see pitfalls). Consecutive quaternion samples are sign-continuous (positive dot product) so that slerp never takes the long way. - Solar-system bodies are supplied as apparent ICRF directions (Skyfield `.apparent()`: light-time, aberration, gravitational deflection), so bodies and stars share one GPU pipeline; refraction is applied client-side (Earth only, toggle). - Babylon.js scene: camera at the origin; celestial sphere radius 1000 units; mapping ENU -> Babylon (left-handed, Y-up): East -> +X, Up -> +Y, North -> +Z. Azimuth is measured from north through east. This mapping exists in exactly one module (`frontend/src/sky/math/frames.ts`) and is unit-tested: az=0° -> +Z, az=90° -> +X, alt=90° -> +Y. - Observer coordinates: on Earth, WGS84 geodetic latitude and east longitude (Skyfield `wgs84.latlon`); elsewhere, planetocentric latitude, east longitude and elevation in metres above the IAU reference ellipsoid of the body (gas giants: 1-bar level), the location being built with `PlanetTopos.from_latlon_distance` and the ellipsoid radius at that latitude (see pitfalls). Responses echo `latitude_kind: "geodetic" | "planetocentric"`. - Equator of date: the backend also supplies, per sample, the rotation ICRF -> true equator and equinox of date (Skyfield `framelib.true_equator_and_equinox_of_date`), used by the frontend for the equatorial grid of date, RA/Dec of date and local apparent sidereal time; precession and nutation are never computed client-side.
architecture.data_flow: 1. Boot: the frontend fetches `/meta`, then the catalogs (stars binary, DSO JSON, constellations JSON, star name index). Catalogs are cached by the browser (ETag + max-age) and parsed into typed arrays once. 2. Scene request: for the current (observer, tt0, speed) the frontend requests one `/sky/frame` covering a time window of `n` samples spaced `step_s` simulated seconds apart, and stores it in a frame buffer. 3. Every animation frame: compute tt; slerp the horizon quaternion between the two surrounding samples (one uniform for all shaders); cubic-Hermite-interpolate body directions, distances, magnitudes and phases with Catmull-Rom tangents from neighbouring samples (directions renormalised after interpolation); recompute labels, lines and culling at <= 10 Hz. 4. Refetch triggers: the buffered window is 70 % consumed (prefetch, seamless), the observer changes, the speed changes by more than a factor of 10 or changes sign (pausing keeps the buffer), the requested body set changes, or tt jumps outside the window. Samples always increase in time (tt0 + i * step_s); for negative speeds the client places tt0 so that the current time sits near the end of the window, and "70 % consumed" is measured in the direction of travel. While a request is in flight, extrapolate from the last two samples so motion never stalls. 5. Speed-adaptive sampling: choose `step_s` (integer seconds, rounded up, minimum 1) so that the window covers about 60 s of real time with n = 32 (step_s = ceil(|speed| * 60 / 32)), then clamp step_s to the smallest class maximum among the requested bodies, using `/meta.limits.max_step_s` (Moon 3600 s, inner planets 21600 s, Sun and outer planets 86400 s, minor bodies 86400 s) so that the client can decide on snapshot mode before requesting. If the resulting window covers less than 5 s of real time (extreme speeds), switch to snapshot mode: n = 1, refetch at <= 4 Hz, no interpolation, and show a "coarse time-lapse" badge. 6. Proper motion of stars is applied in the vertex shader from the catalog's per-star velocity vector and a `years_since_epoch` uniform, so the star catalog is fetched exactly once per session regardless of the date.
architecture.backend: - Python 3.14, FastAPI, application-factory pattern, Pydantic v2 models, settings from environment variables (pydantic-settings). No database. - Lifespan startup loads: timescale; ephemeris (memory-mapped by jplephem, so a 3 GB file costs no RAM per worker); PCK text kernel and Moon frame kernels; the Hipparcos catalog turned into the compact binary star catalog (built once, cached in DATA_DIR); DSO catalog; constellation data; MPC orbit tables (parsed once, cached as Parquet in DATA_DIR). - Compute endpoints are synchronous `def` path operations (FastAPI runs them in its thread pool; NumPy releases the GIL). Run with `fastapi run --workers `; ephemeris pages are shared through the page cache. - All Skyfield calls are vectorized: over the time samples of a frame (a single `Time` array) and over stars (one vectorized `Star` object built with `Star.from_dataframe`). - Minor bodies: Kepler orbits from MPC elements (`sun + mpc.mpcorb_orbit(...)`, `mpc.comet_orbit(...)`), computed only for the objects explicitly requested, with a per-object LRU cache; the request cap is enforced by the API contract and `/minor-bodies/defaults` returns a ranked list no longer than that cap (the reference frontend pins the first 20). - Data bootstrap: a `sky-data` CLI (uv-managed script) downloads every data file into DATA_DIR with SHA-256 verification and resumable downloads; the API also self-bootstraps at startup when files are missing and `SKYAPI_AUTO_FETCH` is true (the default; CI and the test suite set it to false and rely on de440s plus committed excerpts). `/health` reports `starting` with download progress until the app is ready (used by the Docker healthcheck and by the frontend splash screen). - A small in-memory LRU cache of computed frames keyed by the canonicalized query string. No Redis, no external services. - The `astro` package owns every Skyfield object (`loader.py`) and exposes typed functions (`horizon_quaternions`, `body_samples`, `star_catalog`, `altaz`, ...); routers only validate, canonicalize, call and serialize.
architecture.frontend: - React 19 for UI chrome only, plus a framework-agnostic `SkyEngine` class (Babylon.js 9) that receives frames and options from a single simulation store (clock, observer, view options). The store is synchronized both ways with URL query parameters so any view is shareable by copying the URL. - Engine selection: `WebGPUEngine` when `WebGPUEngine.IsSupportedAsync` resolves true, otherwise the WebGL2 `Engine`. Every custom shader must run on both backends. - Rendering layers: (1) stars: a single mesh with four vertices per star and a custom vertex shader (direction + proper motion, quaternion rotation, optional refraction, corner expansion sized by magnitude and field of view, colour from B-V) and a soft-disc fragment shader; never point primitives; (2) deep-sky objects: instanced symbol quads by object type, scaled by angular size with a minimum pixel size; (3) constellation lines (from star positions, so they follow proper motion), IAU boundaries and names; (4) solar-system bodies: billboards with phase shading lit from `sun_dir`, sized by angular diameter with a minimum pixel size; (5) horizon line, cardinal points, altitude/azimuth grid, equatorial grid, ecliptic, meridian; (6) sky background: gradient driven by the Sun's altitude (Earth only), night-vision mode as a red palette post-process over the whole UI; (7) labels: HTML overlay positioned from projected coordinates, throttled and culled by priority; (8) augmented reality: camera video background plus a device-orientation camera, or WebXR immersive-ar when available. - Camera: fixed at the origin, rotation-only controls (drag, touch, inertia), field-of-view zoom (wheel, pinch) from 1° to 120°; keyboard shortcuts for time and view. - Client-side refraction (Earth only, toggle): Sæmundsson's formula (true altitude -> apparent altitude) in the star shader and for interpolated bodies, Bennett's inverse (apparent -> true) where the UI converts back; must match Skyfield's `altaz(temperature_C='standard', pressure_mbar='standard')` within 1′ for altitudes above -1°, verified with committed fixtures. - Performance budget: see non_functional_requirements (60 fps on desktop, >= 30 fps on a 2022 mid-range phone with the full catalog and all layers).
architecture.deployment: - Development: `fastapi dev` for the API and `vite` for the frontend, with the Vite dev server proxying `/api` to the API. HTTPS on the dev server is required for geolocation, camera, device orientation and WebXR on a phone; document how to reach the WSL 2 dev server from a phone on the LAN. - Production-like: Docker Compose with two services: `api` (uvicorn workers) and `web` (nginx serving the built SPA with long-lived cache headers and reverse-proxying `/api` to `api`; TLS terminated by nginx with mounted certificates, or by an external reverse proxy placed in front of `web`, both documented). DATA_DIR is a host directory bind-mounted into `api` (`SKY_DATA_DIR` in `.env`, default `./data`), so `uv run sky-data fetch` on the host and `docker compose run --rm api sky-data fetch` fill the same directory; data is never baked into an image.

api_contract.conventions: - Base path `/api/v1`. All endpoints are GET, stateless and deterministic. Query parameters are canonicalized before computing and before cache lookup: sorted, latitude/longitude rounded to 1e-6° (the reference frontend sends 0.01°, see OBS-7), elevation to 1 m, `tt` to 1e-8 day (about 1 ms), body lists sorted and de-duplicated. The reference frontend also aligns `tt0` to the sample grid (tt0 = floor(tt / step_d) * step_d with step_d = step_s / 86400) so that users watching the same sky at the same time share cache keys; the backend accepts any `tt`. - JSON responses are Pydantic v2 models with complete OpenAPI metadata (descriptions, examples). The frontend's TypeScript types are generated from the OpenAPI document (openapi-typescript) and committed; CI fails if they drift. - Binary responses use `application/octet-stream`, little-endian, a versioned magic header and columnar typed arrays, documented in `docs/api.md` with a byte-layout table. - Caching headers: catalogs -> `Cache-Control: public, max-age=3600, stale-while-revalidate=86400` with a strong ETag (content hash) and `If-None-Match` -> 304; frames and altaz -> `Cache-Control: public, max-age=300`; `/meta` and `/health` -> `no-store`. GZip middleware for responses >= 1 KiB. - Errors follow RFC 9457 (`application/problem+json`: type, title, status, detail, instance, errors[]): 400 invalid parameter, 404 unknown object, 422 outside data coverage (the response carries the valid range), 429 rate limited (`Retry-After`), 503 data not ready (`Retry-After`). - Rate limiting: in-memory token bucket per client IP on compute endpoints (default 20 requests/s, burst 40), configurable through settings. - Units: angles in degrees, distances in astronomical units, time as TT Julian Date unless the field is suffixed `_utc` (ISO 8601, `Z`, proleptic Gregorian, astronomical year numbering), angular sizes in degrees, magnitudes as floats.
api_contract.endpoints:
GET /health -> { status: "starting" | "ready" | "degraded", progress?: { file, downloaded_bytes, total_bytes }, version }
GET /meta -> { api_version, server_time: { tt, utc, tt_minus_utc_seconds }, ephemeris: { name, coverage_tt: [start, end] }, observers: [ { id: "mercury" | "venus" | "earth" | "moon" | "mars" | "jupiter" | "saturn" | "uranus" | "neptune" | "pluto", name_key, frame (SPICE/IAU frame name, e.g. "ITRS", "MOON_ME_DE440_ME421", "IAU_MARS"), radii_km: [a, b, c], latitude_kind: "geodetic" | "planetocentric", coverage_tt: [start, end], approximation_code?: "pluto_barycenter" } ], coverage: { ephemeris_tt: [start, end], delta_t: { observed_tt: [start, end], predicted_until_tt }, iau_rotation_reliable_tt: [start, end], proper_motion_warning_years: 10000, mpc_elements: { warn_years: 2, error_years: 50 } }, bodies: [ { id, kind: "star" | "planet" | "dwarf_planet" | "moon", name_key, radius_km } ], catalogs: { stars: { count, version, etag, epoch_tt, magnitude_limit, license, attribution }, dso: { count, version, etag, license, attribution }, constellations: { count, culture: "modern", etag, license, attribution }, minor_bodies: { asteroids, comets, elements_epoch_range_tt, license, attribution } }, geocoder: { enabled, url, email?, attribution, min_interval_ms }, limits: { max_samples: 64, max_minor_bodies: 100, max_targets: 200, speeds: [ ... ], max_step_s: { moon: 3600, inner_planets: 21600, sun_and_outer: 86400, minor: 86400 } } classes: inner_planets = Mercury, Venus, Mars; sun_and_outer = Sun, Jupiter to Pluto, and Earth when it is a target } Notes: `pluto` as an observer uses the Pluto-system barycenter (flagged by `approximation_code`, translated by the frontend). Coverage of `moon` is bounded by the Moon orientation kernel (1550-2650 with moon_pa_de440). `bodies=all` silently excludes the observer's own body; naming it in an explicit `bodies` list is a 400.
GET /catalogs/stars (binary, format "SKYS" v1) header: magic "SKYS" (4 bytes), version u32 = 1, count u32, epoch_tt f64 (2451545.0 = J2000; Hipparcos positions are propagated from their own epoch J1991.25 to J2000 by Skyfield at build time), flags u32 (reserved, 0) columns, in this order and packed without padding: dir f32[count * 3] ICRF unit vector at the catalog epoch pm f32[count * 3] tangential proper-motion velocity in ICRF, radians per Julian year (parallax and radial velocity ignored; documented) mag i16[count] millimagnitudes, Johnson V (Hipparcos `Vmag`) bv i16[count] B-V in millimagnitudes, 32767 when unknown hip u32[count] Hipparcos identifier Sorted by magnitude ascending so any prefix is a valid brighter-than subset. Build rule, from the vectorized Skyfield `Star` at t = J2000: p0 = star.at(t).position, v = star.at(t).velocity per Julian year, dir = p0 / |p0|, pm = v / |p0|. Shader rule: dir(t) = normalize(dir + pm * years_since_epoch), then aberration dir' = normalize(dir(t) + observer_velocity / c). Parity test: within 0.1″ of Skyfield's astrometric directions and within 1″ of `.apparent()` (gravitational deflection ignored). `mag` is Johnson V (Skyfield's `magnitude` column).
GET /catalogs/stars/index -> [ { hip, names: { proper?, bayer?, flamsteed? }, con } ] named or designated stars only (about 4 000), used for search and labels; proper names are the IAU names and are not translated
GET /catalogs/dso -> [ { id: "NGC7000", names: [ ... ], messier?: 45, type: "galaxy" | "open_cluster" | "globular_cluster" | "planetary_nebula" | "nebula" | "other", ra_deg, dec_deg, mag?, major_arcmin?, minor_arcmin?, pa_deg?, con } ] Subset of OpenNGC: all Messier objects plus NGC/IC objects with mag <= 14 or major axis >= 5′ (limits configurable).
GET /catalogs/constellations -> { culture: "modern", constellations: [ { abbr: "Ori", latin: "Orion", genitive: "Orionis", lines: [ [hip, hip], ... ], boundary: [ [ra_deg, dec_deg], ... ], label: { ra_deg, dec_deg } } ] } Lines reference Hipparcos identifiers so that they follow the rendered stars; boundaries are ICRS J2000 polygons.
GET /minor-bodies/search?q=&limit=20 -> [ { id, designation, name?, kind: "asteroid" | "comet", h_mag?, elements_epoch_tt } ] id syntax: `a:` for numbered asteroids, `a:` for unnumbered ones, `c:` for comets with spaces replaced by `_` (e.g. `c:1P`, `c:C/2023_A3`); ids are URL-safe and used everywhere (frame, altaz, URL `minor` and `sel`) GET /minor-bodies/defaults -> same shape, at most `limits.max_minor_bodies` entries, ranked by expected brightness: asteroids with H <= 9 sorted by H, then comets whose elements epoch lies within 2 years of the server date sorted by proximity of perihelion to the server date.
GET /sky/frame?body=earth&lat=48.8566&lon=2.3522&elev=35&tt=2461285.5&step_s=300&n=32&bodies=all&minor=a:1,c:1P -> { observer: { body, lat_deg, lon_deg, elev_m, latitude_kind, warnings: [ ... ] }, time: { tt0, step_s, n, tt_minus_utc_seconds, utc0, lst_hours?: [ n ], warnings: [ ... ] }, lst_hours = local apparent sidereal time in [0, 24), Earth only; tt_minus_utc_seconds = TT − UTC from 1972 on, TT − UT1 (ΔT) before 1972 when "UTC" means UT1 horizon: { q: [ [x, y, z, w] ... n ] }, ICRF -> ENU, sign-continuous equinox_of_date: { q: [ [x, y, z, w] ... n ] }, ICRF -> true equator and equinox of date, sign-continuous observer_velocity_au_d: [ [x, y, z] ... n ], barycentric velocity of the observer in ICRF, au/day (client-side aberration) sun_dir: [ [x, y, z] ... n ], ICRF unit vector observer -> Sun (phase shading, sky brightness) bodies: [ { id, kind, samples: { dir: [ [x, y, z] ... n ], dist_au: [ n ], mag: [ n ], phase: [ n ], diam_deg: [ n ] }, warnings: [ ... ] } ], minor: [ { id, name, kind, samples: { same }, elements_epoch_tt, extrapolation_years, warnings: [ ... ] } ] } Warnings are objects `{ code, params?, range_tt? }` with a closed list of codes, translated by the frontend, never free text: `observer.warnings` carries `iau_rotation_approximate` and `pluto_barycenter`; `time.warnings` carries `delta_t_approximate` and `proper_motion_extrapolated`; `minor[].warnings` carries `mpc_extrapolation` (beyond `warn_years`) and `mpc_unreliable` (beyond `error_years`, in which case `samples` is null and the object is still listed). Hard coverage limits (ephemeris range, observer frame kernel range) are 422s, not warnings. Rules: 1 <= n <= 64; step_s >= 1; `bodies` is `all` (default) or a comma-separated list; `minor` is an optional list capped by `limits.max_minor_bodies`; the backend clamps `step_s` to the smallest per-class maximum among the requested bodies and reports the value actually used; `n * (bodies + minor)` <= 4096; 422 when the window leaves the coverage of the ephemeris or of the observer frame.
GET /sky/altaz?body=earth&lat=&lon=&elev=&tt=&targets=hip:32349,moon,dso:NGC224,a:1,c:1P&refraction=1 -> [ { id, alt_deg, az_deg, ra_icrs_deg, dec_icrs_deg, ra_date_deg, dec_date_deg, dist_au?, mag?, phase?, diam_deg? } ] target syntax: `hip:`, `dso:` (Messier aliases resolved through the catalog), body ids, `a:`, `c:`; authoritative Skyfield values (refraction only when requested and only on Earth); used by the details panel and by conformance tests. Cap: 200 targets.
GET /sky/events?body=earth&lat=&lon=&elev=&tt=&targets=sun,moon [L] -> rise, set, transit and twilight times for the local day; backlog item tied to INFO-3, not part of M2, documented here only so that the path is reserved.
api_contract.conformance: - `tests/fixtures/` holds machine-generated cases (generator script committed, sources cited): JPL Horizons reference values for a set of bodies, observers and dates, and Skyfield outputs for the same cases. - pytest asserts backend accuracy against Horizons (planets and Moon within 2″, stars within 1″ of the catalog transformed by Skyfield). - vitest loads the same fixtures and asserts that the TypeScript propagation, interpolation, proper-motion and refraction code reproduces Skyfield within tolerance: stars <= 1″, bodies <= 1′ for step_s <= 3600 and |speed| <= 3600. - An OpenAPI snapshot test fails the build when the contract changes unless `docs/openapi.json` and the generated types are updated in the same commit (a deliberate change), and `api_version` in `/meta` follows semver of the contract.

functional_requirements:
Priority tags: [M] must ship in v1; [S] should ship in v1 and may be simplified if it endangers the schedule; [L] later, backlog only (record in docs/backlog.md, do not implement unless trivial).
- OBS-1 [M] When the URL carries no observer, the app requests browser geolocation (secure context only) after a one-line explanation; on success the observer is Earth at the reported latitude, longitude and elevation (0 m when absent). - OBS-2 [M] If geolocation is denied or unavailable, the observer defaults to Greenwich (51.48° N, 0.00° E, 0 m) and the location panel opens. - OBS-3 [M] Manual entry on Earth: latitude and longitude (decimal or DMS, hemisphere letters accepted), elevation in metres, validated with an immediate preview. - OBS-4 [M] Place search on Earth through OpenStreetMap Nominatim, called from the browser and never from the API: explicit submit only (no autocomplete), at most one request in flight, at least 1 s between requests, `format=jsonv2`, `limit=5`, `accept-language` set to the UI language; results show their display name and the attribution "© OpenStreetMap contributors". - TIME-1 [M] Live mode by default, following the wall clock; the time display shows local time, UTC and the TT Julian Date, plus local apparent sidereal time on Earth (interpolated from `time.lst_hours` on the 24 h circle, unwrapping across samples). - TIME-2 [M] A custom date-time editor (native date inputs cannot express years <= 0): integer year field (negative allowed, astronomical numbering), month, day, hour, minute, second, and a local-time/UTC toggle; the editable range is the ephemeris coverage from `/meta`; a proleptic-Gregorian notice appears for dates before 1582-10-15. - TIME-3 [M] Transport controls: play/pause, speed selector (the list from `/meta.limits.speeds`, forward and backward), step buttons (±1 min, ±1 h, ±1 day, ±1 sidereal day on Earth, ±1 year) and "now" (returns to live mode). - TIME-4 [M] Coverage warnings: when the current time is outside the validity of a data source (Moon orientation kernel, MPC elements, ΔT confidence), the affected layer shows a warning badge with the valid range; the time control never leaves the ephemeris range. - TIME-5 [S] Keyboard shortcuts: space (play/pause), `,` and `.` (slower/faster), `[` and `]` (step back/forward), `n` (now), `t` (time editor).

non_functional_requirements.performance: - API: `/sky/frame` p95 < 150 ms for n = 32 with the default body set on one vCPU, < 400 ms with 100 minor bodies; catalogs served from prebuilt files in < 50 ms; `/minor-bodies/search` < 50 ms from an in-memory index holding only designation, name, H and epoch; ready within 60 s of start when data files are present (the star catalog binary is cached on disk); RSS < 1 GB per worker excluding the OS page cache. - Frontend: 60 fps on a desktop with integrated graphics and >= 30 fps on a 2022 mid-range phone (Pixel 6a / Snapdragon 7-series class) with the full catalog and all layers on; catalog parsing < 300 ms; first meaningful sky < 2 s on a warm cache and < 5 s on a cold 4G connection; main JavaScript bundle <= 1.5 MB gzipped, AR/WebXR code split into lazily loaded chunks; no allocations in the per-frame render path; labels and lines updated at <= 10 Hz. - Bandwidth: a session downloads the catalogs once (<= 6 MB compressed), then a few kilobytes per frame request.
non_functional_requirements.accuracy: - Backend against JPL Horizons fixtures: Sun, Moon and planets within 2″; stars within 1″ of Skyfield's own transformation of the catalog; TT, UT1 and ΔT exclusively through Skyfield. - Frontend against backend fixtures: stars <= 1″ (shader and CPU parity with Skyfield), interpolated bodies <= 1′ for step_s <= 3600 and |speed| <= 3600, refraction <= 1′ above -1° altitude. - Live mode drift <= 100 ms relative to the device clock; time-lapse speed exact to 0.1 %.
non_functional_requirements.compatibility: - Browsers: the Vite 8 default target "baseline-widely-available"; last two major versions of Chrome, Edge, Firefox and Safari; iOS Safari 17+ and Android Chrome 120+ on mobile; WebGL2 required, WebGPU used when available; AR sensor mode on iOS and Android, WebXR mode on Android Chromium browsers. - Input: touch, mouse and keyboard; portrait and landscape. - Containers: Dockerfiles must build for linux/amd64 and linux/arm64 (multi-arch base images, no architecture-specific binaries); CI verifies amd64 only; development on WSL 2 (Debian).
non_functional_requirements.security_and_privacy: - HTTPS everywhere in production (terminated by nginx or by an external reverse proxy in front of `web`; plain HTTP is for local development only); strict Content-Security-Policy without inline scripts, `connect-src` limited to the app origin plus the configured geocoder; standard security headers set by nginx; CORS limited to the app origin in production and to the Vite dev origin in development. - No accounts, cookies, trackers, analytics or third-party scripts; no server-side storage of requests; access logs never record query strings or client coordinates; rate limiting keeps IPs in memory only. - Every parameter validated with explicit bounds; request caps from the API contract; dependency audits in CI (`pip-audit` for Python, `npm audit` for Node) with a documented allow-list for accepted advisories.
non_functional_requirements.reliability: - The API answers 503 with `Retry-After` while `starting`; missing optional data (MPC, DSO, constellations) puts it in `degraded` state where only the affected endpoints return 503. - The frontend retries failed requests with exponential backoff and keeps propagating from the last frame; a catalog ETag change triggers a reload prompt. - Downloaded files are verified by SHA-256; corrupted caches are rebuilt automatically at startup.
non_functional_requirements.observability: - Structured JSON logs (timestamp, level, request id, route, status, duration_ms) without personal data; `/health` for probes; a `Server-Timing` header with compute time on frame responses.
non_functional_requirements.accessibility_and_i18n: - WCAG 2.2 AA for the UI chrome; keyboard and screen-reader operable; `prefers-reduced-motion` and `prefers-color-scheme` respected; FR and EN complete at all times (CI fails on missing or unused keys); dates and numbers formatted by Intl.
non_functional_requirements.maintainability: - Strict typing end to end (pyright strict, TypeScript strict, generated API types); the sky mathematics isolated in pure, dependency-free modules with 100 % line coverage: `frontend/src/sky/math`, `frontend/src/state/url`, `backend/src/skyapi/astro/quaternions.py` (matrix to quaternion, NEU to ENU, sign continuity) and `backend/src/skyapi/catalogs/formats.py`; the rest of `astro/` and `catalogs/` >= 90 %; UI components covered by smoke tests; documentation in `docs/` updated in the same commit as the change it describes.
non_functional_requirements.data_freshness_and_footprint: - MPC elements refreshed by running `sky-data update` (a weekly cron line is suggested in the docs), which rebuilds the caches and prints a reminder to restart the API (`docker compose restart api`): a running API only reloads data at startup; it performs no network calls at runtime other than the bootstrap download. - Images: `api` < 400 MB, `web` < 50 MB; the data directory holds about 3.5 GB (de441 3.1 GB, MPCORB about 250 MB, everything else < 100 MB).

data_sources_and_licensing.licensing_policy: - First action of the project: read `LICENSE` and `README.md` at the repository root; record the license identifier in `CLAUDE.md`; keep all application code under that license. If `LICENSE` is missing or unrecognisable, stop and ask. - Third-party data is never committed; the only files allowed in git are (1) test excerpts under 1 MB in `backend/tests/fixtures/excerpts/` with a header stating source and license and an entry in THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md, (2) the small factual CSVs authored for this project (`constellation_names.csv`, `planetary_sites.csv` with its citations), (3) machine-generated test fixtures containing JPL Horizons values (US Government data). Everything else is downloaded at bootstrap, transformed into caches under DATA_DIR, and served by the API with its license declared in `/meta.catalogs..license` and `.attribution`. - `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` at the repository root lists every dataset above with source URL, version or fetch date, license and attribution text; the frontend "About" screen renders the same credits (mandatory for CC BY-SA and OpenStreetMap). - Catalogs derived from share-alike sources (HYG, OpenNGC, Stellarium) are published under the same license; the build scripts are public in the repository, which satisfies the share-alike condition; nothing else in the application is affected. - Never add datasets, images, fonts or textures whose license is unknown or restricted to non-commercial use; prefer public domain, CC0, CC BY, BSD, MIT, ISC or Apache sources.
data_sources_and_licensing.coverage_summary: Reported by `/meta` and enforced by the UI: ephemeris -13200..+17191; Moon-surface observers 1550..2650 (Moon kernel); other bodies use IAU rotation models, exact by definition but with growing physical uncertainty away from J2000 (label "approximate" outside 1800..2200); MPC elements reliable within about 2 years of their epoch (warning beyond 2 years, error beyond 50 years); Hipparcos proper motion is linear and adequate for visualisation over the whole range (warning beyond ±10 000 years); ΔT from historical and IERS tables for -720..present with predictions about one year ahead and a long-term parabola beyond (label "approximate").

engineering_standards.backend_python: - Tooling: uv-managed packaged application (`uv init --package`, src layout, `uv_build` backend); `.python-version` = 3.14; `uv.lock` committed; `uv sync --locked` in CI and Docker; every command through `uv run` (`uv run pytest`, `uv run sky-data fetch`); `[project.scripts] sky-data = "skyapi.cli.sky_data:main"`; development tools in `[dependency-groups] dev`. - Runtime dependencies (latest stable at project start, verified on PyPI): fastapi[standard], skyfield (>= 1.55), numpy, pandas, pyarrow, pydantic-settings. Dev: pytest, pytest-cov, hypothesis, ruff, pyright (httpx comes with fastapi[standard]). Nothing else without an ADR. - Ruff for linting and formatting: line length 100; rule sets E, F, W, I, UP, B, SIM, N, RUF, PT, ANN, with per-file ignores limited to tests. Pyright strict on `src/`, basic on `tests/`. Complete type annotations; no untyped `Any` leaving a public function; NumPy arrays typed with `numpy.typing.NDArray`. - Structure: routers never import Skyfield; `astro/` exposes pure functions that receive `SkyState` explicitly (the frozen dataclass created in lifespan that holds the timescale, ephemeris, planetary constants, frames, catalogs and MPC index); no module-level mutable state apart from the app state created in lifespan; settings read once from the environment with the `SKYAPI_` prefix (DATA_DIR, EPHEMERIS, AUTO_FETCH, WORKERS, RATE_LIMIT_RPS, RATE_LIMIT_BURST, GEOCODER_URL, GEOCODER_ENABLED, GEOCODER_EMAIL, CORS_ORIGINS, LOG_LEVEL). - Errors: typed exception classes mapped to RFC 9457 responses by a single handler; never a bare `except`; explicit bounds on every parameter. - Logging: stdlib `logging` with a JSON formatter (no third-party logging library), request-id middleware, no query strings or coordinates in logs. - Tests: pytest markers `unit`, `api`, `conformance`, `slow`; `de440s.bsp` downloaded once into a cached test DATA_DIR; hypothesis property tests for canonicalization, time conversions and the SKYS round-trip; coverage >= 90 % on `skyapi/astro` and `skyapi/catalogs`; API tests through `TestClient`; an OpenAPI snapshot test.

workflow.per_milestone: - Plan first (plan mode), then implement in small steps; run the relevant tests after every step and `make check` before every commit; update the documentation in the same commit as the change. - When an API or a version behaviour is uncertain, consult the official documentation before writing code: the Context7 and DeepWiki MCP servers if configured in `.mcp.json`, otherwise fetch the official docs (Skyfield: rhodesmill.org/skyfield; FastAPI: fastapi.tiangolo.com; Babylon.js: doc.babylonjs.com; Vite: vite.dev; Tailwind: tailwindcss.com; uv: docs.astral.sh/uv). Never guess signatures; prefer official docs over blog posts. - Use subagents for independent, precisely described work (for example "implement the SKYS parser and its tests against backend/tests/fixtures", "generate the Horizons fixtures", "review this milestone against the acceptance list and report gaps") and for an adversarial review at the end of each milestone; give each a narrow scope and an explicit list of files it may touch. - Keep the context small: never print catalogs or data files; use `head`, `wc`, targeted greps and Python one-liners; compact the conversation after each milestone; `docs/plan.md` is the durable memory across sessions. - Record every notable decision as an ADR (context, options, decision, consequences) and every deviation from the brief in `docs/backlog.md` with its reason. - Commit at least once per milestone with the prescribed message; never `--no-verify`; never skip, weaken or mark as expected-failure a test to make a gate pass; if a gate cannot pass, fix the cause or document the exception in the commit body and in docs/plan.md.

pitfalls.skyfield_and_backend: - Skyfield's altaz rotation matrix (`GeographicPosition.rotation_at`, `PlanetTopos.rotation_at`) maps ICRF to a LEFT-handed frame: x = north, y = east, z = zenith (determinant -1). Swap rows x and y to obtain the right-handed ENU matrix before converting to a quaternion, and validate in tests that `atan2(E, N)` reproduces Skyfield's `altaz()` azimuth and `asin(U)` its altitude. - Both `rotation_at` methods accept `Time` arrays (extra trailing dimension); build one `Time` array per frame with `ts.tt_jd(array)` and vectorize everything; never loop over samples in Python unless a specific call proves scalar-only (then loop over at most 64 samples and note it). - `altaz(temperature_C=..., pressure_mbar=...)` uses Earth's refraction model and raises for observers on other bodies: request refraction only when the observer is Earth. Skyfield refraction is what the client-side formula must match. - Calendar: Skyfield's default `julian_calendar_cutoff = None` is the proleptic Gregorian calendar; set it explicitly and test 1582-10-04/1582-10-15. `utc_datetime()` and `utc_iso()` raise on negative years; produce ISO strings yourself from `t.utc` calendar tuples with astronomical year numbering (year 0 exists, `-0044-03-15` style with a signed 4+ digit year). - DE441 has two segments per target: requires Skyfield >= 1.51 (1.55 is fine). The file is memory-mapped; never read it into memory or into your context. `de440s` covers 1849-2150 only: tests must not request dates outside it. - Observer on another body: `PlanetaryConstants.build_latlon_degrees` raises `ValueError("only spherical bodies are supported")` for every body whose PCK radii differ (Mars, the giant planets, ...). Build the location yourself: `PlanetTopos.from_latlon_distance(frame, Angle, Angle, Distance)` with distance = radius of the IAU ellipsoid at the planetocentric latitude plus elevation, then `body + topos`; keep `build_latlon_degrees` only where radii are equal (Moon). Build frames from `pck00011.tpc` (`IAU_MARS`, `IAU_JUPITER`, ...) and, for the Moon, from the frame kernel plus the binary PCK (`MOON_ME_DE440_ME421`); check the kernel coverage and return 422 outside it. `bodies=all` excludes the observer's own body; naming it explicitly (the Moon from the Moon) is a 400. - Vectorized stars: one `Star.from_dataframe(df)` for the whole catalog; drop rows with NaN coordinates; Hipparcos positions carry the catalog epoch J1991.25 (`epoch_year` in the dataframe); the SKYS builder must evaluate the vectorized Star at J2000 (position and velocity) and derive `dir` and `pm` from those vectors, otherwise every star is offset by 8.75 years of proper motion (up to 90″ for Barnard's star). Skyfield's loader keeps the positional columns and `magnitude` (Johnson V); check whether `B-V` is present and otherwise read that field from the pipe-separated `hip_main.dat` yourself. - MPC: `load_mpcorb_dataframe` on the full file takes minutes and lots of memory; do it once in `sky-data build-caches`, store Parquet, keep only the search index in RAM. Comets have several orbit solutions per designation: sort by `reference` and keep the last, as in the Skyfield documentation. Use `skyfield.constants.GM_SUN_Pitjeva_2005_km3_s2` consistently for every Kepler orbit. - FastAPI: CPU-bound path operations must be plain `def` (thread pool), not `async def`; return binary catalogs with `FileResponse` from the cache directory (zero-copy) plus ETag; do not use the deprecated `ORJSONResponse`; `GZipMiddleware(minimum_size=1024)`; in-memory rate limiting is per worker process (document it); `fastapi run --workers N` for production. - Equator of date: `skyfield.framelib.true_equator_and_equinox_of_date.rotation_at(t)` is a proper rotation (determinant +1) that converts directly to the `equinox_of_date` quaternion; RA/Dec of date for `/sky/altaz` come from `.radec(epoch=t)`, ICRS values from `.radec()`; local apparent sidereal time is the RA of date of the zenith direction (validate against Skyfield's `t.gast` plus the east longitude). - Observers: the Sun is not an observer (no meaningful `sun_dir`, phases or lighting); observing from a body that is also requested as a target is a 400. - Canonicalization must happen before cache lookup and before computation, and the response must echo the canonical values so that the client and the server agree on the cache key. - The star catalog and the DSO catalog are built at `build-caches` time and versioned by a content hash that becomes the ETag; never rebuild them per request.
pitfalls.babylon_and_frontend: - WebGPU has no variable point size: never rely on `PointsCloudSystem` or `pointSize`; draw stars as camera-facing quads (four vertices per star in one mesh, corners expanded in the vertex shader). - Provide WGSL shaders for WebGPU (`shaderLanguage: ShaderLanguage.WGSL`) and GLSL for WebGL2; under WebGPU, GLSL shaders trigger a runtime download of glslang/twgsl wasm from a CDN, which the strict CSP forbids. Create the engine with `EngineFactory.CreateAsync` or `WebGPUEngine.IsSupportedAsync` plus `initAsync`, and test both paths in Playwright. - ES6 tree-shaking requires side-effect imports for the features used (e.g. `@babylonjs/core/Materials/shaderMaterial`, raw-texture and WebXR feature modules); missing imports surface as "... is not a function" at runtime. Keep the list in one file with a comment per import. Never import `@babylonjs/core/Legacy/legacy` or the UMD `babylonjs` package. - Babylon is left-handed and Y-up by default; keep it and implement the ENU mapping (East +X, Up +Y, North +Z) in `sky/math/frames.ts` only, with unit tests for the three cardinal cases; azimuth increases clockwise seen from above. - Camera at the origin: use a rotation-only camera (custom inputs with inertia); the field of view in Babylon is vertical and in radians; `maxZ` must exceed the sky-sphere radius; in WebXR the experience helper resets the camera to the origin on session start, so the sky sphere must follow the XR camera position every frame (or be parented to it) while ignoring its translation. - Aberration in the star shader: dir' = normalize(dir + v / c) with v the backend `observer_velocity_au_d` and c = 173.1446 au/day (first order; error below 0.01″); never apply it to solar-system bodies, whose directions are already apparent. - Compute the horizon quaternion on the CPU in float64 and upload it as a uniform; do not accumulate rotations on the GPU. Float32 is fine for unit vectors (about 0.02″) and for `pm * years` over the whole ephemeris range (about ±15 200 years around J2000). - `DeviceOrientationEvent.requestPermission()` on iOS must be called from a user gesture in a secure context; use `deviceorientationabsolute` on Android and `webkitCompassHeading` on iOS; apply `screen.orientation.angle`; convert (alpha, beta, gamma) with the W3C intrinsic Z-X'-Y'' order; verify with fixtures. - `getUserMedia({ video: { facingMode: { ideal: "environment" } } })`; the `` needs `playsinline` and `muted`; stop all tracks on exit. - Geolocation, camera, sensors and WebXR require a secure context: the Vite dev server runs HTTPS via `@vitejs/plugin-basic-ssl`; the phone must trust the certificate or use the browser's insecure-origin exception (documented in docs/dev-wsl2.md), and WSL 2 needs mirrored networking or a port proxy to be reachable on the LAN. - Vite 8: use `build.rolldownOptions.output.codeSplitting` (no `manualChunks` object form); `@vitejs/plugin-react` 6 transforms with Oxc (no Babel plugins unless `@rolldown/plugin-babel`); import shaders with `?raw`; only `import.meta.env.VITE_*` variables reach the client. - Tailwind 4: no `tailwind.config.js`; class names must appear as complete literal strings (no runtime concatenation) or they are not generated; the night variant is `@custom-variant night (&:where([data-mode=night], [data-mode=night] *))`. - React 19 StrictMode double-invokes effects in development: engine creation must live in an effect with a cleanup that disposes it, and must be idempotent. - URL state: update with `history.replaceState` at <= 2 Hz while the user drags or time flows; round floats (coordinates 0.01°, alt/az 0.01°, fov 0.1°, tt 1e-6 day) to keep URLs short; parse defensively. - Dates: JavaScript `Date` parses negative years badly; build dates with `Date.UTC` and `setUTCFullYear`, keep TT Julian Date as the canonical value, and format years with an explicit sign; `Intl` formats negative years only with an era option, so provide a custom formatter for the time display. - Nominatim: browsers cannot set `User-Agent`; identification relies on `Referer` — add `` — plus the optional `email` parameter; handle HTTP 403/429 with a clear message; never call it on every keystroke. - Labels: an HTML overlay updated with `transform: translate3d` and a fixed pool of elements avoids layout thrash; cap the number of visible labels. - Docker: never bake data into images; give the `api` healthcheck a long `start_period` (first-start caches) and let `web` depend on `api` being healthy; in nginx serve `index.html` with `no-cache` and hashed assets with `immutable`; enable gzip for JSON and the binary catalog.
